contracts.description: The MCP adapter contract: the pure dispatch function over (tool-call, filesystem snapshot) -> result envelope. Owns spec-source resolution and its inline-vs-path precedence, totality (every thrown library or load error mapped to a structured {ok:false,error,detail} result, never propagated), and the result shape each tool returns. The verb cores are felag-core's contract; a tool that is a pure pass-through to a conformant core is specced only at its adapter boundary, never re-stated.

exclusions: The verb semantics themselves: lint, verify, audit, promote, graduate, render, prime, hash, fmt, and the author-class validators are spec/felag-core's contract (felag-ts CONFORMS). This contract never re-states them; a tool that is a pure pass-through is specced only at its adapter boundary (I/O resolution + result wrapping + error mapping).

The MCP transport: stdio framing, JSON-RPC, the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk wiring, the tools/list and tools/call envelopes, and how a host renders a result. The contract is the pure dispatch function; the server is an un-specced binding over it, exactly as CLI output formatting is non-core in felag-core.

Tool input JSON Schemas as advertised to a host (each tool's MCP inputSchema): advisory ergonomics, observable but undeclared. The contract gates on dispatch behavior given an input, not on the schema a host uses to build that input.

Filesystem access: how the server reads a specDir from disk is transport. The contract models the filesystem as an explicit path->content snapshot passed to dispatch, so path-loading is a pure, fixturable function; real file I/O lives in the server binding.

Statefulness: audit's optional work-layer wiring (spec/felag-tasks) is stateful; the audit tool exposes only the pure coverage projection with no work layer attached. Work mutation through MCP is out of scope.

MCP adapter residue at 0.1.0: E_LIB is the catch-all for any felag-core library throw not classified as E_PARSE. Its triggers depend on felag-core's INCIDENTAL throwing behavior, which felag-core does not make contractual: serialize's CS6 refusal of a non-finite number (itself unfixturable — a JSON fixture cannot encode the value whose refusal it would pin), or a core verb throwing on a degenerate input (e.g. verify on a spec with no preamble, or render given an out-of-enum audience). Because none of these throws is a felag-core guarantee, none can be pinned by a stable cross-implementation fixture; the obligation rides on prose and the dispatch implementation. The fixturable, contractually-stable totality case is E_PARSE; that dispatch maps a non-McpError throw to E_LIB rather than propagating it is pinned by a reference-implementation unit test, not a contract fixture.
goals: Expose the felag toolchain's verbs as MCP tools so any agent drives felag conversationally — lint a spec, verify conformance, run the author-class validators, promote, graduate — without shelling out to the CLI.

Pin the adapter surface, not the verbs: a second MCP implementation in any language conforms by matching the pure dispatch function's behavior, while reusing whatever felag-core implementation it already has for the verb semantics.
Keep the adapter total and honest: every thrown library or load error becomes a structured result, and the model is never asked to trust an MCP server that crashed instead of answering.
spec.name: felag-mcp

spec.body:
Every MCP tool call resolves through a single pure function, mcpDispatch(call, fs), where call is {tool, input} and fs is a filesystem snapshot (below). It returns a result envelope: a discriminated union of {ok:true, result} on success and {ok:false, error, detail} on failure. result is the tool's payload (the verb's result, possibly adapter-shaped); error is a stable machine code (E_*); detail is a required non-empty human-readable string whose WORDING is non-normative but whose presence and type are normative.

Dispatch is TOTAL: it never throws and never propagates an exception to the transport. The error partition is closed and a second implementation MUST match the CODE: E_UNKNOWN_TOOL (the tool name is absent from the registry); E_NO_SPEC_SOURCE and E_SPEC_NOT_FOUND (spec resolution, see it-mcp-resolve); E_BAD_INPUT (a REQUIRED input is absent — asOf/implementation for verify and audit, asOf/transition for promote, criterionId/implementation for graduate, audience for render, output for validate_prime, or neither records nor text for fmt); E_PARSE (interchange that does not parse, whether the fmt text or a snapshot file); and E_LIB (the catch-all for any other thrown felag-core library error). The error CODE is the divergence point; this totality is the verify-is-a-ledger stance (felag never crashes the caller) carried to the tool layer.

Two partition rules a stranger needs to reproduce the codes exactly. Ordering: EVERY required input for the tool — scalar or object, e.g. asOf, transition, audience, output, criterionId, implementation — is checked BEFORE spec-source resolution, so when a call lacks both a required input AND a spec source, E_BAD_INPUT precedes E_NO_SPEC_SOURCE/E_SPEC_NOT_FOUND (felag_render with no inputs is E_BAD_INPUT on audience, not E_NO_SPEC_SOURCE). Nullity: for a required input, a JSON null is treated as absent (E_BAD_INPUT), identically to a missing key — a present null is never forwarded to a verb.

The presence/validity line is deliberate: the adapter checks only that a required input is PRESENT (a structural check it can make without verb knowledge) and maps absence to E_BAD_INPUT; an input that is present but semantically invalid (e.g. an out-of-enum render audience) is the core verb's to reject, and the core rejecting it by throwing surfaces as E_LIB — the adapter does not re-implement the verb's input validation.

The twelve tools mirror the felag-core library verbs: felag_lint, felag_fmt, felag_hash, felag_verify, felag_audit, felag_promote, felag_graduate, felag_render, felag_prime, felag_validate_author, felag_validate_excavate, felag_validate_prime. Eight have a CLI verb of the same stem; the four author-class validators (render and the three validate_*) expose felag-core library functions with no CLI counterpart. Most tools are pure pass-throughs whose result is the named felag-core function's return wrapped unchanged under {ok:true, result}; those are specced here only at the envelope boundary, never re-stated (their semantics are felag-core's). A pass-through success fixture therefore EMBEDS a concrete felag-core result by reference: that value is pinned by the core's own contract and is expected to move if the core's result legitimately evolves under it — the fixture asserts the adapter wraps it unchanged, not that the value is itself a c-mcp obligation.
spec.title: Dispatch and the result envelope

spec.body:
Tools that operate on a spec accept the spec inline under `spec` (a SpecRecord array) and/or by path under `specDir` (a directory). The name `spec` is deliberate: `records` is reserved for the EVIDENCE channel (verify/audit take VerificationRecords, graduate takes JudgmentRecords) and would otherwise collide with the spec — so a single call may legitimately carry BOTH an inline `spec` (the contract) and a `records` array (the evidence), and they never contend. Resolution is deterministic: inline `spec` WINS when present — where PRESENT means `spec` is a JSON array (any other type is treated as absent and falls through) — and specDir is not consulted. Otherwise specDir is loaded from the filesystem snapshot by reading specDir + '/spec.jsonl' and specDir + '/fixtures.jsonl' — either file may be absent, and whichever are present have their records concatenated (parity with the CLI's loadSpecDir). If neither file is present in the snapshot, resolution fails with E_SPEC_NOT_FOUND. If neither `spec` nor `specDir` is supplied at all, resolution fails with E_NO_SPEC_SOURCE.

The filesystem is an explicit snapshot — a map from logical 'dir/file' path (joined with '/') to file content — passed to dispatch, NOT a live disk read. This makes path-loading a pure, fixturable function: a fixture carries its own in-memory filesystem. The real MCP server populates the snapshot by reading the requested specDir from disk before calling dispatch; that disk I/O is transport, excluded from this contract. The precedence rule (inline beats path) is the load-bearing decision: it lets an agent compose or test against an inline spec while the path remains the ergonomic default.
spec.title: Spec-source resolution: inline-vs-path precedence

spec.body:
Three tools return a result that is NOT a bare pass-through of a single core function — the adapter composes or reshapes, and that shaping is contract:

felag_lint returns {valid, errors, orphanFixtures}: the core lint result (valid, errors) plus orphanFixtures, the ascending set of fixture ids referenced by no criterion. The CLI emits this as a stderr warning; the adapter surfaces it in-band. An orphan is a warning, never a lint error — valid stays true.

felag_hash returns {hashes}, an array of {id, hash} for the FIXTURE records only (other record types are skipped), ascending by id, hash being felag-core's fixtureHash (CS9). An optional fixtureId narrows to one fixture. This is the CLI's hash iteration surfaced as structured data.

felag_fmt returns {canonical}, the canonical serialization of the input — given inline records, or given raw text it parses then re-serializes (the round-trip primitive). When BOTH records and text are present, records WINS and text is consulted only when records is absent — the same inline-structured-wins tiebreak as resolveSpec's spec-over-specDir. It is READ-ONLY: unlike the CLI's in-place fmt, the tool never writes a file. This is structural, not incidental — dispatch is handed no writer, so no tool can mutate the filesystem.

The adapter is thin: each tool delegates verb semantics to the felag-core library and adds only I/O resolution, result shaping, and error mapping. It never re-derives or alters a verb's result. (This thinness is a judgment seam, recorded descriptive — documented, never gated.)
spec.title: Adapter-shaped tool results

spec.gherkin:
Given a valid call to any pass-through tool (render, verify, audit, promote, graduate, prime, validate_author, validate_excavate, validate_prime)
When mcpDispatch routes it
Then the envelope is {ok:true, result} and result is the named felag-core function's return wrapped unchanged — the adapter resolves I/O and wraps, it neither re-derives nor reshapes a pass-through result
And the spec resolves from the `spec`/`specDir` channel while evidence (where the verb takes it) rides the `records` channel

Given a call naming a tool absent from the registry
When mcpDispatch routes it
Then the envelope is {ok:false, error:'E_UNKNOWN_TOOL'} with a non-empty detail, and nothing is thrown

Given a call whose input drives a felag-core function to throw (felag_fmt over unparseable text)
When mcpDispatch routes it
Then the throw is caught and mapped to {ok:false, error:'E_PARSE'} with a non-empty detail — dispatch never propagates the exception
And any other non-mapped library throw maps to the E_LIB catch-all (residue: its triggers depend on felag-core's incidental throwing behavior, none contractually stable — see exclusions)

Given a tool call missing one of its REQUIRED inputs (verify with a spec but no implementation; fmt with neither records nor text; render with a spec but no audience; promote with a spec and transition but no asOf; render with an explicit null audience)
When mcpDispatch routes it
Then the envelope is {ok:false, error:'E_BAD_INPUT'} naming the missing input in detail — absence is a structural check the adapter makes without verb knowledge, a JSON null counts as absent, and E_BAD_INPUT precedes spec-source codes whenever a required input AND the spec source are both absent — for EVERY tool, whether its required input is a scalar (verify with no inputs), an object (promote with only asOf, missing transition), or the tool takes a spec plus one scalar (render or validate_prime with no inputs at all)
And this is distinct from E_LIB (a present-but-invalid input the core rejects by throwing)

Given a call carrying BOTH an inline spec (valid) and a specDir whose snapshot files are broken
When the tool resolves its spec
Then the inline spec is used and the specDir is not consulted — the result reflects the inline spec, not a parse error
And given an inline `spec` that is NOT a JSON array (treated as absent) alongside a valid specDir, resolution falls through to the path

Given a call carrying only a specDir, whose snapshot holds spec.jsonl and fixtures.jsonl
When the tool resolves its spec
Then both files are read and their records concatenated (loadSpecDir parity) and the tool runs against the merged spec

Given a call carrying only a specDir whose snapshot spec.jsonl is present but unparseable
When the tool resolves its spec
Then the envelope is {ok:false, error:'E_PARSE'} — the snapshot-file parse site, distinct from fmt's text parse, also maps to E_PARSE rather than swallowing a partial load

Given felag_verify carrying BOTH an inline spec (the contract) and a records array (passing VerificationRecords, the evidence)
When the tool runs
Then the spec resolves from `spec` and the records are consumed as EVIDENCE, not as spec — the conformance report reflects the evidence against the inline contract
And an implementation that read the spec from `records` (as the CLI's verify reads a records.jsonl positional) would misverify here

Given felag_lint over a lint-valid spec that contains TWO fixtures referenced by no criterion, supplied out of id order
When the tool runs
Then the result is {valid:true, errors:[], orphanFixtures:[both ids, ascending]} — the orphans are warnings surfaced in-band (valid stays true), and the ascending order is discriminated
And given a lint-INVALID spec (a duplicate criterion id) the core errors flow through UNCHANGED under {valid:false, errors:[...]} while orphanFixtures is still computed — the adapter never short-circuits the orphan scan on an invalid spec

Given felag_hash over a spec containing non-fixture records and two fixtures whose ids are NOT in input order
When the tool runs
Then the result is {hashes:[{id, hash}]} for the fixture records only, ascending by id (the sort is discriminated), hash being felag-core's fixtureHash
And given an optional fixtureId, only that fixture's hash is returned

Given felag_fmt over non-canonical raw text
When the tool runs
Then the result is {canonical} carrying the canonical serialization (parse then serialize) and no file is written
And given BOTH records and text, records wins (the inline-structured-wins tiebreak) and the text is not consulted

Each tool delegates verb semantics to the felag-core library and adds only I/O resolution, result shaping, and error mapping; it never re-implements, re-derives, or alters a verb's result. Recorded descriptive — a documented seam that never gates.

*End of protocols. Validate your outputs: `lint` for interchange, the author-output/excavate-output formats for authored records, the promotion-input format for ratification. Fixtures carry the contract; prose carries intent.*
